case_name: Nagar Council, Kapurthala v Davinder Singh and Others
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows:
The appellants herein in raising all contentions before the Labour Court if and when such applications are filed.
In Civil Appeal No. 5873 of 2006 disposed of on 15.12.2006, this Court observed as under:

For establishing their claim that they were entitled for wages for working on Saturdays and Sundays, the workmen must establish their legal right in the proceedings under Section 33-(C) (2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
The High Court in its impugned judgment has held as under:

In view of the circumstances afore noticed, we dispose of this petition with a direction to the respondents to pass appropriate orders computing the amount due to the petitioners in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court (supra) and pay the same within a period of three months from today.
The High Court in the impugned judgment has noticed that now octroi is again being levied and in that view of the matter issued the impugned directions.
petitioner_arguments: They will have to establish the same.
In such a proceeding, undisputedly the appellants shall be entitled to raise all contentions before the Industrial Court.
The claim of the petitioner is hardly disputed in the written statement so as to make them entitled to receive the said payment.
court_reasoning: We are of the opinion that for establishing their claim that they were entitled for wages for working on Saturdays and Sundays, the workmen must establish their legal right in the proceedings under Section 33-(C) (2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
In this view of the matter, we are of the opinion that it is not necessary for us to interfere with the impugned judgment at this stage.
We may notice that in Civil Appeal No. 5873 of 2006 disposed of on 15.12.2006, this Court observed as under:
holding: Leave granted in special leave petitions.
